title: BHOPAL
subtitle: The Night the City Woke
intro: A pesticide plant vented methyl isocyanate over Bhopal at midnight. The gas lasted one night; the argument over who counted has lasted four decades.
lede: A 2:01 film in 9 scenes and 37 shots, built from 23 procedural sets, 35 sourced lines and 10 authored transitions. Every frame rendered on free GitHub Actions hardware.

stats.label: sourced lines
stats.note: every line carries a source id

cut.heading: 37 shots across 9 scenes.
cut.body: The final cut runs 2:01 at 24 fps; the average shot is 3.3 seconds. 27 of the 37 joins are hard cuts. The other 10 are authored transitions (iris, match cut, dissolve, paper wipe, whip, dip). The scene list below is generated from the release timeline, not the storyboard.

motion.heading: The edit has a grammar.
motion.body: The grammar is mechanical-causality. The signature moves are listed below. Transition counts come from the final edit manifest.
signature: needle match: gauge needle to clock hand
valve iris: handwheel rim to flare ring to court seal
water/flame match: tap drip to memorial flame
gas haze: dissolve only where gas is the subject
siren whip: horn to street lamp with a pre-lapped siren
paper edge: ledger and newspaper wipe the frame

families.name: Iris
families.use: A lamp or valve closes to a circle, moving the eye to the next object.

families.name: Match cut
families.use: The same shape or object at a new scale.

families.name: Dissolve
families.use: Used only where two images belong to the same thought.

families.name: Paper wipe
families.use: A printed edge carries the next set into frame.

families.name: Whip
families.use: A fast pan carries the cut across connected spaces.

families.name: Dip
families.use: A held gap between two arguments.

families.name: Hard cut
families.use: The default join. Used where softening would weaken the argument.

items.title: The Bhopal disaster and its aftermath: a review

pipeline.heading: Every frame is assembled on GitHub.
pipeline.body: Blender, Piper, Chromium and ffmpeg run on a free Ubuntu CPU runner. The owner's machine writes the code; it does not render the film. The pipeline is public, repeatable and allowed to fail loudly.

items.title: Source lock
items.body: The storyboard is a JSON contract. Every narration line names a source. The validator refuses unsourced lines, missing shots and filler before a runner is allowed to render.

items.title: Procedural sets
items.body: Blender 4.2 builds the film's sets as still plates. No stock images.

items.title: Narration
items.body: Piper reads the script locally with en_US-lessac-medium. No cloud narration, no per-word billing, no API key in the repository.

items.title: Camera and type
items.body: Chromium drives the timeline frame by frame: push-ins, pans, match cuts, mask wipes, impact cards and captions. The camera is code, so every frame is repeatable.

items.title: Score and master
items.body: ffmpeg synthesises the score, mixes the narration, burns the SRT into the master and encodes the MP4.

items.title: Free CI
items.body: The render runs on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu CPU. No GPU. No paid runner. The owner's machine writes the code; it does not render the film.

record.heading: What the record shows.
record.body: Each entry is taken from the release itself: the timeline, the edit manifest and the independent QC report. A dossier that only shows the final cut is a portfolio, not a process.

items.title: Source lock
items.body: 35 narration lines across 5 sources. Every line in the final timeline resolves to a source in the release metadata; the validator refuses a line without one.

items.title: Final cut
items.body: 9 scenes, 37 shots, 2:01. Average shot 3.3s. 27 hard cuts and 10 authored transitions.

items.title: Independent QC
items.body: Passed: -1.8 dBTP wanted no higher than -1; I -12.8 LUFS wanted -16.5 to -11; median 45.8 dB wanted at least 36 dB, worst 43.5 dB at S08; 36 cues in bhopal-gas-tragedy.srt; median edge/interior 1.08 wanted at most 1.75.

items.title: Release
items.body: Release film-bhopal-gas-tragedy-final-26 carries the 1080 master, SRT, thumbnail, timeline, edit manifest and script. The site deploys only the 720 preview.

build.heading: The render is public.
build.body: Recent Film pipeline runs, read from the public GitHub API. The workflow log is part of the record.

credits.heading: Who did what.
credits.body: The same free, local toolchain on every film: no paid API, no GPU and no stock footage.
rules: Every narration line carries a source id. The render fails if a line, shot or source is missing.
No number on screen without a source or an explicit attribution.
No stock footage. Every set is procedural.
No paid API keys. The pipeline runs on free CI.
If the edit is weak, the render does not ship.
credits.quote: “If the edit is weak, the render does not ship.”

scenes.title: The city
scenes.purpose: Open on a sleeping city, then land the date and the title without a lecture.

narration.text: Bhopal, 2 December 1984.
A city sleeps beside a pesticide plant.

scenes.title: The plant
scenes.purpose: Establish the factory as a place of work and a place of storage, not a monster.

narration.text: The Union Carbide plant made pesticides for Indian farms.
Its tanks held methyl isocyanate, a chemical that attacks the lungs.
Tank 610 held about forty-two tonnes of it.
The safety systems were not all working.

scenes.title: The warning
scenes.purpose: Make the failure mechanical and legible: water, pressure, a shut refrigeration unit, an offline flare.

narration.text: The official inquiry found water had entered Tank 610.
Pressure and temperature climbed.
The refrigeration unit had been shut down.
The flare tower was offline, and the scrubber could not cope.
No public warning prepared the city.

scenes.title: The release
scenes.purpose: Move the gas through the city without reconstructing death; the sound carries the scale.

narration.text: Around midnight, the tank vented.
A cloud of MIC rolled low over the railway colony and the old city.
People woke with burning eyes and no breath.
They ran into the dark, away from a smell they could not name.
The gas moved through the streets before the city understood.

scenes.title: The count
scenes.purpose: Put the numbers on screen with their sources and their disagreements intact.

narration.text: The official immediate death toll was 2,259.
Madhya Pradesh later confirmed 3,787 deaths.
Survivors' clinics estimate 8,000 died in the first weeks, and 8,000 more since.
More than 500,000 people were exposed.

scenes.title: The settlement
scenes.purpose: Follow the claim from the courtroom to the ledger, and show what a settlement does not settle.

narration.text: In 1989, the Supreme Court approved a $470 million settlement.
The claims were consolidated under the Indian government.
Union Carbide's chairman was charged in India, but never extradited.
In 2010, seven former employees were convicted. The sentence was two years.
The settlement did not end the argument.

scenes.title: The water
scenes.purpose: Bring the disaster into the present through the tap, the sample and the body.

narration.text: The plant stopped production in 1986.
Its waste and contaminated water remained.
Survivors still carry the exposure in their bodies.
Groundwater near the site is still contaminated.

scenes.title: The memory
scenes.purpose: Move from the archive to the memorial without turning the dead into decoration.

narration.text: Every year, Bhopal remembers.
The disaster helped push India's Environment Protection Act in 1986.
It did not settle the question of who was responsible.
The memorial is a wall, a flame, and an unfinished argument.

scenes.title: The claims
scenes.purpose: Close on a sentence, not a spectacle.

narration.text: The gas lasted one night.
The claims have lasted four decades.
